purpose: Freeze a deterministic one-dimensional axial-momentum residual curve derived only from the checksum-tracked NASA Wind-US reference solution. Experimental exit Mach, pressure, and temperature data are not used in the derivation and remain independent benchmark observations.

section_reduction.geometry_pressure_term_definition: dJ_geometry = p_bar * dA, where p_bar is the arithmetic average of adjacent area-weighted section pressures and dA is the source-backed quasi-1D area change
section_reduction.note: The residual is what remains after subtracting the source-backed quasi-one-dimensional pressure-area momentum contribution from the exact NASA reference axial momentum-flux change. It is therefore a reference-derived effective axial force closure, not a Darcy friction coefficient or experimentally measured wall shear.

normalization.duplicate_policy: Axial stations duplicated at adjacent zone interfaces are grouped by x rounded to 12 decimal places and arithmetic-averaged before J, p_bar, and the cumulative residual are formed.
normalization.endpoint_policy: The first station is frozen at x=0 m and the final station at the source-backed geometry exit x=0.356 m; the raw extracted exit coordinate differs only by approximately 4.57e-8 m.

line_momentum_closure.interpolation: piecewise-linear interpolation of the frozen I(x) curve at solver cell faces
line_momentum_closure.conservation_property: The discrete integral sum(Fprime_mom_net * dx) equals mdot_1d * [I(x_exit)-I(x_start)] up to floating-point roundoff.
line_momentum_closure.mass_flow_policy: mdot_1d is computed from the one-dimensional inlet state and inlet area. The closure preserves the NASA reference solution's specific axial-momentum residual while avoiding a forced match to the two-dimensional reference mass flow.
line_momentum_closure.sign_semantics: Signed axial line force: positive adds streamwise momentum to the gas; negative removes streamwise momentum.

independence_and_claim_boundary: No experimental exit Mach, pressure, or temperature point is used to construct I(x) or Fprime_mom_net.
The closure is computational-reference-derived and may support a reduced-order thermal/flow benchmark only.
It is not a measured friction coefficient, wall-shear distribution, chemistry model, species model, or LBW/YBW criterion.
